strategy.summary: Anticipate the extreme (High or Low) of the week forming on a high-volatility news day (typically Tuesday or Wednesday) as price stings into a HTF PD array. Ride the weekly expansion until Thursday/Friday, then trade a TGIF reversal sweeping Thursday's extreme if the trend is exhausted.

timeframes.notes: Bias relies on Daily levels and the economic calendar. Entries can be taken on the 1H or 15m timeframes once the daily sweep occurs.

other: Economic calendar news events for volatility injection

glossary.TGIF: Thank God It's Friday; a weekly profile setup where Friday sweeps Thursday's extreme and reverses back into the weekly range to cap the week.
glossary.One shot one kill: Catching the majority of the weekly range by taking generally one macro trade per week.
glossary.Cap the week: Establishing the final absolute low or high of the week on Thursday or Friday, concluding the weekly expansion phase.
glossary.Turtle soup: A false breakout or liquidity sweep of a previous day's extreme (e.g., sweeping Thursday's low before reversing higher).

custom_signals.plain_definition: The 0.2 and 0.3 Fibonacci retracement levels drawn from the low to the high of the current week's range, indicating where Friday will likely close.

sequence: Check Monday's price action to see if it consolidates or stings into a HTF PD array.
Identify when high-impact news occurs on the economic calendar to anticipate the week's volatility injection.
Watch for price to sting into a HTF premium or discount array on the high-volatility day (often Tuesday or Wednesday) to form the absolute extreme (High/Low) of the week.
Trade the continuation trend (One shot one kill) on Wednesday and Thursday targeting opposite HTF liquidity pools or PD arrays.
At the end of Thursday, if the daily candle lacks displacement and closes poorly, anticipate the trend is exhausted.
On Friday, wait for a TGIF setup: a turtle soup sweep of Thursday's low/high, then enter the reversal to rebalance the weekly range.

invalidation.text: If Monday simply expands without coming into a premium array and Thursday is nowhere near a PD array, blindly guessing a standard weekly template is invalid.

filters.text: At the end of Thursday, do not chase price or take new continuation trades in the weekly trend direction if the market has already expanded a lot of pips.
Never establish a rigid weekly template on Sunday and blindly stick to it; you must react and adapt to daily closes and news.

entry_rule.text: For the TGIF setup, enter on a lower timeframe (e.g., 15m) when Friday sweeps Thursday's extreme (turtle soup) and reverses back into the range.
entry_rule.quote: Previous day low sweep, turtle soup, boom we continue higher on the 15 minute.

target_rule.text: For the weekly expansion, target a higher timeframe liquidity pool. For the TGIF Friday reversal, target an unmitigated fair value gap or order block to rebalance the weekly range.
target_rule.quote: Either on a Thursday or a Friday we will target to rebalance something inside the weekly range.

stop_rule.text: No explicit stop rule mentioned in this specific video.

management.notes: Once the TGIF target (rebalancing a gap inside the range) is hit, exit completely and do not look for new setups.

presenter_claims.claim: Consistently catching a 2.74 R trade on a weekly basis outperforms a lot of hedge funds.

strategy.notes: The presenter emphasizes that structural market delivery is dynamic. The 'Tuesday High/Low' is a common profile, but CPI/News on Wednesday can easily shift the profile to a Wednesday High/Low. Traders must rely on the economic calendar rather than fixed day-of-week assumptions.

setup_walkthrough.what_happens: Monday establishes a range, leaving a Daily FVG. Tuesday stings into this Daily FVG to form the high of the week.
Price trends downward through Wednesday and Thursday, presenting 1H continuation trades targeting a discount liquidity pool.
Thursday's daily candle closes poorly without showing strong downward displacement, signaling trend exhaustion.
On Friday, price sweeps Thursday's low (Previous Day Low) to create a 'turtle soup' reversal setup.
The TGIF reversal trades back up into the weekly range, specifically targeting a 4H FVG/Order Block overlap to rebalance.

examples.presenter_commentary: The presenter stresses reading the daily candles. He emphasizes that if Thursday lacks displacement, you should avoid shorting on Friday and instead look for a TGIF reversal after a previous day low sweep.

setup_walkthrough.what_happens: DXY trades into a Daily FVG and overlapping 4H mitigation block to establish the low of the week.
Price expands higher toward a clearly defined FVG target, arriving on Thursday.
Thursday caps the week with no huge displacement. On Friday, DXY fails to sweep Thursday's high, forming SMT divergence with EURUSD (which did sweep its extreme).
